habitat: Pairs and small flocks in thornveld and mixed bushveld, especially dry country with baobabs and large thorn trees, where they build communal nests. Patchily distributed and nomadic when not breeding.
summary: A fairly common resident. Both sexes have a red bill. The male is blackish-brown, with white edges to the wing feathers. The female is paler on the breast. White feathers show on the flanks and shoulders. The immature is greyish and mottled, the bill starting horn-coloured, then dull yellow, then orange. The call at the nest is a chatter and a mellow triddlyoo trill. The Kemp paper name Redbilled Buffalo Weaver and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Thick-billed Weaver has a heavy black or horn bill, not a red bill, and the female is streaked below.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is nomadic when not breeding. The sexes share the red bill. The female is only described as paler on the breast. No flight photograph was found. A frame that only showed a camera screen was not used. Population figures and the Kemp name Redbilled Buffalo Weaver were left unchanged.
